cycles.explanation: Miami, Ohio State, Ole Miss, Georgia, Texas, Texas A&M, Notre Dame, Iowa, Alabama, Vanderbilt, Oklahoma, Michigan, Washington, Louisville, Illinois, USC, LSU, Penn State, Pittsburgh, Georgia Tech, Clemson and Florida State form a loop: following every head-to-head result among them leads back to where it started, so no ordering can honour all 48 of them. The weakest link was Louisville's 24-21 win over Miami (+5.4 adjusted margin; the winner rates 7.5 points worse on the power ratings; the loser fared better against 3 shared opponents. Since then: Louisville has more losses, 4 to 3; Louisville has lost 3 since against Miami's 2; Miami's wins since average 7.9 rating points better; so the resume order decides how far apart they sit), so it was set aside, along with 4 other results in this loop.

Texas Tech, BYU, Utah, Iowa State, TCU, SMU, Houston, Arizona and Arizona State form a loop: following every head-to-head result among them leads back to where it started, so no ordering can honour all 19 of them. The weakest link was Arizona State's 26-22 win over Texas Tech (a 4-point win at home is worth +1.6 once venue is accounted for; the winner rates 12.0 points worse on the power ratings; the loser fared better against 3 shared opponents. Since then: Arizona State has more losses, 5 to 2; Arizona State has lost 3 since against Texas Tech's 1; so the resume order decides how far apart they sit), so it was set aside, along with 2 other results in this loop.

source.attribution: Data: CollegeFootballData.com -- betting lines, play-by-play PPA, and Strength of Record, Strength of Schedule and FPI via ESPN

stages: Stage 1 - rank every team by what it has achieved and how good it is: 0.55 x Strength of Record + 0.3 x market neutral-field rank + 0.15 x opponent-adjusted points added per play (all national ranks, lower is better).
Stage 2 - adjust for how your losses actually look: the venue and margin of each defeat, the quality of your best win, and how comfortably you win.
Stage 3 - when a result spans more than 15 places, pull both teams 0.5 of the way to their midpoint; the upset says both were mis-rated.
Stage 4 - reorder so as few head-to-head results as possible are contradicted, weighing each result by how convincing it was against how far a team would have to move.
Stage 5 - report every contradiction loop and every overridden result, so nothing is hidden.
methodology.summary: base = 0.55 x SoR + 0.3 x Mkt + 0.15 x PPA; pool 40; H2H strength 14, drift exponent 1.5; upset regression on (gap 15, 0.5)
